about: Century Therapeutics is a Philadelphia clinical-stage biotechnology company developing allogeneic cell therapies derived from induced pluripotent stem cells, including natural killer and T cell products for cancer and autoimmune disease. It listed on Nasdaq as IPSC in 2021 and has collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, with no approved product and no meaningful product revenue. Crunchbase shows about 755 million dollars raised. A research-stage company with no consumer brand and minimal sponsorship relevance.

COMPASS Pathways is a London-based mental health biotechnology company developing psilocybin therapy, COMP360, for treatment-resistant depression and post-traumatic stress disorder, delivered alongside psychological support in clinical settings. It listed on Nasdaq as CMPS in 2020, runs Phase 3 trials in Europe and North America, and has no approved product yet. Crunchbase shows about 771 million dollars raised. It has some public profile because of interest in psychedelic medicine, but is not a consumer brand.

Crescent Biopharma is a Waltham, Massachusetts biotechnology company developing oncology antibody drugs, led by a bispecific antibody that targets PD-1 and VEGF for solid tumours, and antibody-drug conjugates. It became a Nasdaq-listed company in 2025 through a merger with GlycoMimetics and financing from investors. It has no approved product and no revenue. Crunchbase shows about 710 million dollars raised. A research-stage business with no consumer brand.

about: Dainippon Sumitomo Pharma, renamed Sumitomo Pharma in 2022, is an Osaka pharmaceutical company in the Sumitomo Chemical group, selling drugs for psychiatry, neurology, oncology, urology and other areas, including the antipsychotic Latuda and the prostate-cancer drug Orgovyx via its Sumitomo Pharma America unit. It also develops regenerative medicine and iPS cell therapies. It is listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, with revenue of several hundred billion yen. B2B pharma with little consumer brand awareness outside Japan.

DocMorris, formerly Zur Rose Group, is a Swiss-based online pharmacy and healthcare group, headquartered in Frauenfeld, that sells prescription and over-the-counter medicines, health products and cosmetics to consumers in Germany, Switzerland and other European markets, with a large pharmacy in Heerlen in the Netherlands and a role in Germany's e-prescription. It has millions of active customers and sales in the high hundreds of millions of francs. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange as DOCM. A recognised consumer health brand in Germany and German-speaking Europe.

Element Biosciences is a San Diego company, founded in 2017, that makes DNA sequencing instruments and chemistry, including the AVITI benchtop sequencer, sold to research institutions, clinical laboratories, pharma and genomics service providers. It earns income from instruments, consumables and software. It is privately held, with Crunchbase showing about 678 million dollars raised from investors such as Foresite and Fidelity. A B2B life-sciences tools company with a high profile in genomics but no consumer awareness.

Fresenius Medical Care is a German healthcare group, based in Bad Homburg, and the world's largest provider of kidney dialysis, running roughly 3,900 dialysis clinics and treating around 290,000 patients, and manufacturing dialysis machines, dialysers and related products. Revenue is close to 20 billion euros and it has about 120,000 employees. It is listed on the Frankfurt exchange as FME and was majority-owned by Fresenius SE until a 2023 restructuring. B2B and patient-facing healthcare, with a corporate rather than consumer brand.

Integra LifeSciences is a Princeton, New Jersey medical technology company selling neurosurgery products such as dural grafts, tissue ablation and monitoring, and tissue technologies including skin and wound repair products like Integra Dermal Regeneration Template, to hospitals and surgeons worldwide. It was founded in 1989, has thousands of employees and revenue of around one and a half billion dollars, and is listed on Nasdaq as IART. B2B and medical, with little consumer awareness.

Jade Biosciences is a Waltham, Massachusetts biotechnology company developing antibody therapies for autoimmune and kidney diseases, led by an anti-APRIL antibody aimed at IgA nephropathy. It became listed on Nasdaq in 2025 following a merger with Aerpio Pharmaceuticals and a venture financing round. It has no approved product and no revenue. Crunchbase shows about 725 million dollars raised, although that figure may include the public financing. A research-stage company with no consumer brand.

about: Larimar Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company in Bala Cynwyd, Pennsylvania, developing nomlabofusp, a protein replacement therapy for Friedreich's ataxia, a rare inherited neuromuscular disease. It listed on Nasdaq as LRMR in 2020 through a merger with Zafgen and has no approved product or revenue. Crunchbase shows about 722 million dollars raised. It has visibility mostly with patient communities and specialist investors, and no consumer brand profile.

mAbxience is a Madrid-based biopharmaceutical company, part of the Insud Pharma group, specialising in developing and manufacturing biosimilars and complex biologic drugs, such as monoclonal antibodies for cancer and autoimmune diseases, with plants in Spain and Argentina. Customers are pharmaceutical partners and healthcare systems that license or buy its products and contract services. Crunchbase shows about 750 million dollars of financing. B2B, with little consumer brand awareness.

MapLight Therapeutics is a Redwood City, California clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing treatments for neurological and psychiatric disorders, with a lead drug, ML-007, a muscarinic receptor agonist for schizophrenia and Alzheimer's disease psychosis. It listed on Nasdaq as MPLT in 2025 and has no approved product or revenue. Crunchbase shows about 791 million dollars raised. A research-stage biotechnology company with no consumer brand and no obvious sponsorship fit.

Maze Therapeutics is a South San Francisco biopharmaceutical company applying human genetics to develop precision medicines for kidney and metabolic diseases, led by MZE829 for APOL1-mediated kidney disease and a programme for Pompe disease with Shionogi. It listed on Nasdaq as MAZE in 2025 and has no approved product, relying on investor funding and licensing deals. Crunchbase shows about 796 million dollars raised. A research-stage biotechnology company with no consumer brand awareness and little sponsorship relevance.

Mirador Therapeutics is a San Diego biotechnology company launched in 2022 with a large venture round, developing precision medicines for immune-mediated and inflammatory diseases such as inflammatory bowel disease and skin and lung conditions. Its founders and backers include ARCH Venture Partners and other major life-sciences investors, and it is run by experienced drug developers. It has no approved product. Crunchbase shows about 730 million dollars raised. A private research-stage firm with no consumer profile.

about: NewLimit is a biotechnology company in the San Francisco Bay Area, founded in 2021 by Brian Armstrong, Blake Byers and Jacob Kimmel, developing epigenetic reprogramming therapies intended to restore youthful function to cells and tissues, starting with liver and immune cells. It is privately held and backed by Coinbase's Armstrong and other investors, with Crunchbase showing about 682 million dollars raised. It has no product revenue. A longevity research company with a profile among technology and venture investors, but little general public awareness.

Odyssey Therapeutics is a Boston-area biotechnology company developing small-molecule and other drugs for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases and cancer, with a platform using chemistry and computational tools to build precision immunomodulators, and clinical programmes in conditions such as ulcerative colitis. It is privately held and backed by life-sciences investors, with Crunchbase showing about 725 million dollars raised. It has no approved product. A research-stage biopharma company with no consumer brand and little sponsorship fit.

about: OPKO Health is a Miami diversified healthcare company, led by billionaire Phillip Frost, with a diagnostics business that included BioReference Health, a large US clinical laboratory partly sold off in 2024, and a pharmaceutical arm with the product Rayaldee for secondary hyperparathyroidism and the pipeline of long-acting growth hormone with Pfizer, plus the ModeX biologics unit. It is listed on Nasdaq as OPK. Customers are hospitals, doctors and health systems. A B2B healthcare company with limited consumer brand awareness.

Pharvaris is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company with offices in Zug, Switzerland and Leiden, the Netherlands, developing oral bradykinin B2 receptor antagonists, led by deucrictibant, to treat and prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema. It is listed on Nasdaq as PHVS and has no approved product. Crunchbase shows about 866 million dollars of funding. Its audience is specialist doctors and patients with a rare disease, and it has no consumer brand profile.

Phathom Pharmaceuticals is a biopharmaceutical company in Florham Park, New Jersey, that markets Voquezna (vonoprazan), a potassium-competitive acid blocker approved in the US for erosive esophagitis, heartburn and H. pylori infection, sold to gastroenterologists and primary care doctors. It was founded in 2018 with Takeda's licence and listed on Nasdaq as PHAT in 2019. Crunchbase shows about 790 million dollars raised. A pharma brand aimed at prescribers and patients, with some direct-to-consumer advertising but modest awareness.

Rakuten Medical is a San Diego biotechnology company, part of the Rakuten group led by Hiroshi Mikitani, developing Alluminox, a photoimmunotherapy platform that uses a light-activated antibody-drug conjugate to attack tumours, and its first product, ASP-1929, which was approved in Japan in 2020 for head and neck cancer. It runs trials in the US, Europe and Asia and funds itself mainly through Rakuten and investors, with Crunchbase showing about 847 million dollars raised. A B2B pharma company; the parent Rakuten is a very visible sports sponsor, but this unit is not.

Rapport Therapeutics is a Boston clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing precision neuroscience medicines that target receptor-associated proteins, with a lead drug, RAP-219, for focal epilepsy and other neurological conditions. It was founded in 2021, listed on Nasdaq as RAPP in 2024, and has no approved product or revenue. Crunchbase shows about 850 million dollars raised. A research-stage business with no consumer brand profile.

Savara is an Austin, Texas biopharmaceutical company developing molgramostim, an inhaled treatment for autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, a rare lung disease. It is listed on Nasdaq as SVRA, has filed or planned a regulatory submission for the drug, and has no marketed products yet. Crunchbase shows about 747 million dollars raised, a figure that may include public financing. A small specialty company with no consumer brand profile, and no real sponsorship fit.

Senseonics is a Germantown, Maryland medical device company that makes the Eversense implantable continuous glucose monitoring system for people with diabetes, a sensor placed under the skin for up to six months or a year with a smartphone app and a wearable transmitter. Customers are diabetes patients and clinicians in the US and Europe, with distribution through Ascensia Diabetes Care and later direct sales. It trades on NYSE American as SENS. Crunchbase shows about 761 million dollars raised. A niche health brand with modest consumer awareness.

about: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries is India's largest drugmaker, headquartered in Mumbai, founded in 1983 by Dilip Shanghvi, making generics, specialty drugs such as Ilumya for psoriasis, and branded products sold across India, the United States, emerging markets and Europe. It acquired Ranbaxy in 2014 and Taro Pharmaceutical, and has revenue of several billion dollars and tens of thousands of employees. It is listed on the NSE and BSE as SUNPHARMA. Mainly B2B and doctor-facing, with moderate consumer awareness at home.

Supernus Pharmaceuticals is a Rockville, Maryland specialty pharmaceutical company focused on central nervous system conditions, selling Qelbree for ADHD, Gocovri and Osmolex for Parkinson's disease, Oxtellar XR for epilepsy and other products, and after acquisitions, the Parkinson's disease treatment Apokyn. Customers are neurologists and psychiatrists, and revenue is several hundred million dollars. It is listed on Nasdaq as SUPN. A prescription-drug business, with little consumer brand profile beyond direct-to-consumer ads.

Sutro Biopharma is a South San Francisco clinical-stage oncology company that develops antibody-drug conjugates and other protein therapeutics using its cell-free manufacturing platform, XpressCF, and has partnerships with companies including Astellas and Bristol Myers Squibb. Its lead programme is luveltamab tazevibulin for ovarian cancer. It is listed on Nasdaq as STRO and has no approved product. Crunchbase shows about 747 million dollars raised. A B2B research-stage business with no consumer profile.

Tarsus Pharmaceuticals is an Irvine, California biopharmaceutical company, listed on Nasdaq as TARS, that markets Xdemvy (lotilaner), the first US-approved treatment for Demodex blepharitis, a mite-related eyelid condition, sold through eye-care professionals and promoted with direct-to-consumer advertising. It was founded in 2016 and has grown to hundreds of millions of dollars in annual sales. Crunchbase shows about 836 million dollars raised. It has some consumer marketing presence in the US, but is not a household brand.

Tessera Therapeutics is a Somerville, Massachusetts biotechnology company, founded by Flagship Pioneering in 2018, developing gene writing technology that can make precise changes to DNA and RNA, aimed at genetic diseases such as sickle cell disease and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, using lipid nanoparticle delivery. It is privately held and has no approved product. Crunchbase shows about 773 million dollars raised. A research-stage company with no consumer brand profile.

Twist Bioscience is a South San Francisco company, founded in 2013, that manufactures synthetic DNA using silicon-based chips, selling genes, oligo pools, NGS target-capture panels and DNA data storage services to pharma, academic and industrial customers. It listed on Nasdaq as TWST in 2018, has annual revenue of a few hundred million dollars and operates factories in California and Oregon. A B2B life-sciences supplier with no consumer profile.

Tyra Biosciences is a Carlsbad, California clinical-stage oncology company developing precision cancer drugs aimed at FGFR genes, including TYRA-300 for bladder cancer and for achondroplasia. It uses structure-based drug design to tackle resistance mutations. It was founded in 2018, listed on Nasdaq as TYRA in 2021, and has no approved product. Crunchbase shows about 756 million dollars raised. A research-stage business with no consumer brand awareness.

UroGen Pharma is a biopharmaceutical company in Princeton, New Jersey, with research operations in Israel, that develops treatments for urothelial and bladder cancers, using its RTGel technology to make drugs that stay in the urinary tract. Its products include Jelmyto for low-grade upper tract urothelial cancer and Zusduri for bladder cancer. It is listed on Nasdaq as URGN. Crunchbase shows about 730 million dollars raised. A specialty drug company selling to urologists with little consumer recognition.

Viatris is a global pharmaceutical company based in Pittsburgh, formed in 2020 by merging Mylan with Pfizer's Upjohn unit. It sells branded and generic medicines including Lipitor, Viagra, Norvasc, Xanax, EpiPen and many biosimilars, in more than 165 countries, with annual revenue of roughly 14 billion dollars and about 32,000 employees. It is listed on Nasdaq as VTRS. Customers are pharmacies, health systems and governments. Some consumer-known brand names, but the corporate name is relatively unknown.

Vor Biopharma is a Cambridge, Massachusetts clinical-stage biotechnology company that was founded in 2015 to develop engineered hematopoietic stem cells for blood cancers, and in 2025 shifted its focus to telitacicept, a drug for autoimmune diseases licensed from RemeGen of China. It is listed on Nasdaq as VOR. It has no approved product. Crunchbase shows about 823 million dollars raised. A research-stage business with no consumer brand profile.

Zenas BioPharma is a Waltham, Massachusetts biopharmaceutical company developing immune-mediated disease treatments, mainly obexelimab for IgG4-related disease, multiple sclerosis and lupus, and other licensed assets from partners in China and Japan. It was founded in 2021 and listed on Nasdaq as ZBIO in 2025. It has no approved product. Crunchbase shows about 813 million dollars raised. A research-stage company with no consumer brand profile and little sponsorship fit.

Achieve Life Science is a Bothell, Washington and Vancouver-based clinical-stage pharmaceutical company developing cytisinicline, a plant-derived treatment for nicotine dependence, for smoking cessation and vaping cessation. It is listed on Nasdaq as ACHV. It has completed Phase 3 trials and has submitted the drug for FDA review, and has no approved product yet. Crunchbase shows about 567 million dollars raised, though this may include public financing. Public health relevance, but no consumer brand yet.

Adlai Nortye is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in Hangzhou, China, with operations in the US, developing cancer drugs including the PI3K inhibitor buparlisib for head and neck cancer, and immuno-oncology candidates. It listed on Nasdaq as ANL in 2023 and has no approved product. Crunchbase shows about 583 million dollars raised. A research-stage company, known only to specialists and investors, with no consumer brand awareness.

about: Ardelyx is a Waltham, Massachusetts biopharmaceutical company selling Ibsrela, a drug for irritable bowel syndrome with constipation, and Xphozah, a phosphate absorption inhibitor for kidney dialysis patients, with a Tenapanor technology and partnerships with Kyowa Kirin and Fosun. It is listed on Nasdaq as ARDX and has revenues of a few hundred million dollars. Crunchbase shows about 608 million dollars raised. A specialty-pharma brand known to doctors, with limited consumer awareness.

Assembly Biosciences is a South San Francisco clinical-stage biotechnology company developing antiviral drugs for hepatitis B and hepatitis D and for herpes, including collaborations with Gilead. It is listed on Nasdaq as ASMB and has no approved product, funding itself through collaborations and equity financing. Crunchbase shows about 658 million dollars raised. A small research-stage company with no consumer brand profile.

Atara Biotherapeutics is a Thousand Oaks, California biotechnology company developing off-the-shelf T-cell immunotherapies, including Ebvallo (tabelecleucel) for EBV-positive post-transplant lymphoproliferative disease, approved in Europe and with US review ongoing, partnered with Pierre Fabre. It is listed on Nasdaq as ATRA and has small revenue, mostly from collaborations. Crunchbase shows about 567 million dollars raised. A specialty biotech with no consumer brand awareness.

Aurinia Pharmaceuticals is a biopharmaceutical company, incorporated in Canada with headquarters in Edmonton and operations in Rockville, Maryland, that sells Lupkynis (voclosporin), a treatment for lupus nephritis, mainly in the United States, Europe and Japan. It is listed on Nasdaq as AUPH and generates annual revenue of a couple of hundred million dollars. Crunchbase shows about 662 million dollars raised. A specialty drug company selling to nephrologists and rheumatologists with little consumer brand awareness.

Avalo Therapeutics is a Rockville, Maryland clinical-stage biotechnology company, formerly Cerecor, developing treatments for immune-mediated diseases, including an anti-IL-1 beta antibody being studied for hidradenitis suppurativa. It is listed on Nasdaq as AVTX, and has no approved product after selling or discontinuing earlier programmes. Crunchbase shows about 663 million dollars raised. A small research-stage company, known mainly to specialist investors and doctors, with no consumer profile and little relevance as a sponsorship prospect.

about: Carbon Health is a San Francisco healthcare company, founded in 2015, that runs primary and urgent care clinics across the US, combined with a mobile app for booking, telehealth and records, and billed to patients and health insurers. It operated roughly 100 or more clinics in states including California, Washington and Texas and was backed by investors such as Blackstone and Anthos Capital, with Crunchbase showing about 642 million dollars raised. It had financial difficulties in the mid-2020s. A recognised regional healthcare brand but not a mass national consumer name.

Colossal Biosciences is a Dallas-founded genetic engineering company, listed here with an Austin address, working on de-extinction and conservation, with programmes to bring back the woolly mammoth, the thylacine and the dodo, and in 2025 announced the birth of animals described as dire wolves. It was founded in 2021 by entrepreneur Ben Lamm and Harvard geneticist George Church, raised hundreds of millions of dollars at a valuation above 10 billion dollars, and has spun out companies. It has a strong media profile and public fascination, though not a consumer product brand.

CStone Pharmaceuticals is a Shanghai-headquartered biopharmaceutical company founded in 2015, developing and commercialising cancer drugs in China and abroad, including the PD-L1 antibody sugemalimab (Cejemly), approved in China, the EU and other markets, and several in-licensed products such as the RET inhibitor pralsetinib. It is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange as 2616 and has revenue from product sales and licensing. Crunchbase shows about 607 million dollars raised. A B2B pharma company with no consumer profile.

Helus Pharma is a biopharmaceutical company in Toronto, Ontario, tagged on Crunchbase under biotechnology and health care, with about 622 million dollars of funding shown and the latest round in September 2026. about: Inhibrx is a San Diego clinical-stage biotechnology company that was spun out in 2024 when Sanofi acquired its INBRX-101 programme, and is now an independent Nasdaq-listed company, Inhibrx Biosciences, listed as INBX, focused on cancer drugs, led by ozekibart (INBRX-109) for chondrosarcoma. It uses a multi-specific antibody platform and has no approved product. Crunchbase shows about 595 million dollars raised. A research-stage business with no consumer profile.

Inovio Pharmaceuticals is a Plymouth Meeting, Pennsylvania biotechnology company developing DNA medicines delivered with its CELLECTRA electroporation device, with a lead product candidate, INO-3107, for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis. It also worked on a COVID-19 vaccine candidate in 2020. It is listed on Nasdaq as INO and has no approved product. Crunchbase shows about 600 million dollars raised. A research-stage company, publicly known in 2020 for its vaccine work, but without a consumer brand.

KALA BIO is a Massachusetts clinical-stage biotechnology company, formerly Kala Pharmaceuticals, developing KPI-012, a cell-secreted protein therapy for persistent corneal epithelial defects and other eye surface diseases. It sold its marketed eye products, Eysuvis and Inveltys, to Alcon in 2022. It is listed on Nasdaq as KALA and has no marketed products. Crunchbase shows about 581 million dollars raised. A small specialist ophthalmology company with no consumer profile.

Karyopharm Therapeutics is a Newton, Massachusetts oncology company that sells Xpovio (selinexor), an oral drug for multiple myeloma and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and is running trials in myelofibrosis and endometrial cancer. It sells to oncologists in the United States and through partners in Europe and Asia. It is listed on Nasdaq as KPTI and has annual revenue of around 150 million dollars. Crunchbase shows about 637 million dollars raised. A specialty drugmaker with no consumer brand awareness.

Korsana Biosciences is a biotechnology company based in Waltham, Massachusetts, tagged under biopharma and biotechnology, that, according to Crunchbase, develops THETA-enabled antibodies. Funding shown is about 555 million dollars, with the latest round in September 2026. The input does not describe its drug programmes, clinical stage, investors or ownership, and it is not otherwise recognised here. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

It is privately held and has no approved product. Crunchbase shows about 563 million dollars raised. A research-stage company with no consumer brand profile and little sponsorship relevance.

about: Mesoblast is a Melbourne regenerative medicine company developing allogeneic cell therapies from mesenchymal precursor cells for inflammatory conditions, such as Ryoncil (remestemcel-L) for children with steroid-refractory acute graft-versus-host disease, approved by the US FDA in late 2024. It also targets heart failure and back pain. It is listed on the Australian Securities Exchange as MSB and on Nasdaq as MESO. Crunchbase shows about 627 million dollars raised. A specialty biotech with a profile among investors, but not consumers.

Monte Rosa Therapeutics is a Boston biotechnology company developing molecular glue degraders, small molecules that make cells break down disease-causing proteins, for cancer, autoimmune and inflammatory diseases, with partnerships including Roche and Novartis. It was founded in 2019 and listed on Nasdaq as GLUE in 2021. It has no approved product. Crunchbase shows about 649 million dollars raised. A research-stage company with no consumer brand recognition.

Obsidian Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company developing tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) cell therapies for cancer, engineered with a controllable interleukin-15 signal that is switched on by an oral drug, to improve the persistence of the cells in solid tumours. It is privately held, with no approved product. Crunchbase shows about 675 million dollars raised. A research-stage firm with no consumer brand awareness.

about: Relmada Therapeutics is a Coral Gables, Florida clinical-stage biotechnology company that was focused on REL-1017 (esmethadone) for depression, which failed in late-stage trials in 2024, and has since pivoted to oncology with NDV-01 for bladder cancer and to other assets. It is listed on Nasdaq as RLMD and has no approved product. Crunchbase shows about 566 million dollars raised. A small research-stage company with no consumer brand profile.

Spero Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing anti-infective drugs, led by tebipenem HBr, an oral carbapenem antibiotic for complicated urinary tract infections, partnered with GSK, and also SPR720 for lung infections. It is listed on Nasdaq as SPRO and has no approved product, with revenue from collaborations. Crunchbase shows about 549 million dollars raised. A B2B research-stage company with no consumer profile.

TriGemX Bio is a biotechnology company in New York, according to Crunchbase, that uses the science of gut-brain biology to create new treatments for health conditions. Funding shown is about 581 million dollars, with the latest figure in October 2026. The input does not describe its drug programmes, stage, investors or ownership, and the funding figure may not be accurate. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Amgen is a US biotechnology company headquartered in Thousand Oaks, California, listed on Nasdaq (AMGN), founded in 1980. It sells biologic medicines including Enbrel, Prolia and Xgeva, Repatha, Otezla, Aranesp and Tezspire, plus biosimilars, and bought Horizon Therapeutics in 2023 for about $28 billion. Customers are hospitals, pharmacies and health systems worldwide. Revenue is around $33 billion with roughly 28,000 employees. It is a very large pharma brand, known to doctors and investors more than the general public.

Amicus Therapeutics is a US biotechnology company based in Princeton, New Jersey, and listed on Nasdaq (FOLD). It specialises in rare metabolic and lysosomal diseases, selling Galafold, an oral treatment for Fabry disease, and Pombiliti plus Opfolda, a combination therapy for late-onset Pompe disease. Customers are specialist physicians, hospitals and patients in the US, Europe, Japan and other markets. Revenue is roughly $500 million to $600 million a year, with total funding of about $2.6 billion. Known mainly to rare-disease doctors and investors, with no consumer brand awareness.

Ascendis Pharma is a Danish biopharmaceutical company based in Hellerup, near Copenhagen, listed on Nasdaq (ASND). It uses its TransCon prodrug technology to create longer-acting versions of drugs, with products including Skytrofa (weekly growth hormone) and Yorvipath (hypoparathyroidism), approved in 2024, and Sanofi-partnered and other programmes in development. Customers are specialist physicians and patients in the US and Europe. Revenue is growing from a low base, with accumulated funding of about $1.9 billion. B2B pharma with no consumer brand profile.

BioCryst Pharmaceuticals is a US biotechnology company based in Durham, North Carolina, and listed on Nasdaq (BCRX). Its main product is Orladeyo (berotralstat), a once-daily oral therapy to prevent attacks in hereditary angioedema, sold in the US, Europe, Japan and other markets, with other rare disease drugs in development. Revenue is a few hundred million dollars a year. Total funding of about $1.8 billion is shown. Known to specialist doctors and rare-disease patients, with no mainstream consumer profile.

Cerevel Therapeutics was a Boston-based clinical-stage neuroscience biotechnology company developing treatments for Parkinson's disease, schizophrenia and epilepsy, led by the Parkinson's candidate tavapadon. It was acquired by AbbVie in August 2024 in a deal valued at about $8.7 billion, and no longer trades independently. Originally launched in 2018 with backing from Bain Capital and Pfizer. It had no commercial products at the time of the sale. B2B pharma development company with no consumer brand profile.

Mirati Therapeutics was a San Diego-based oncology biotechnology company known for Krazati (adagrasib), an oral KRAS G12C inhibitor approved in 2022 for certain lung and colorectal cancers. Bristol Myers Squibb acquired it in January 2024 for about $4.8 billion upfront, so it is now part of BMS. It sold to oncologists and cancer centres in the US, with total funding of about $2.6 billion before the sale. Specialist pharma with no consumer brand awareness.

PacBio (Pacific Biosciences of California) is a life sciences instrument company based in Menlo Park, California, and listed on Nasdaq (PACB). It makes long-read DNA sequencing systems, notably the Revio and Sequel platforms using HiFi sequencing, and sells instruments, consumables and services to genomics labs, universities, pharma and clinical researchers worldwide. It was founded in 2004 and has revenue of roughly $150 million to $200 million, with losses. Well known among scientists, but no consumer visibility.

Reata Pharmaceuticals was a Plano, Texas biopharmaceutical company that developed Skyclarys (omaveloxolone), the first approved treatment for Friedreich's ataxia, cleared by the FDA in early 2023. Biogen acquired Reata in September 2023 for about $7.3 billion, so it is now part of Biogen. Customers were neurologists and rare disease patients. Total funding was about $2 billion before the acquisition. Specialist pharma with no consumer brand recognition.

Roivant Sciences is a biopharmaceutical holding company, based in New York with a UK origin, listed on Nasdaq (ROIV). It builds subsidiary biotech companies called Vants, including Immunovant (immunology antibodies), Priovant (brepocitinib), and previously Dermavant, whose Vtama cream was sold to Organon, and Telavant, sold to Roche in 2023 for about $7 billion. Founded by Vivek Ramaswamy in 2014. Funding of about $2.5 billion is shown. Known to investors and the biotech industry, not to consumers.

Bio-Rad Laboratories is a life science research and clinical diagnostics company based in Hercules, California, listed on the NYSE (BIO) and founded in 1952. It makes laboratory instruments and reagents, including Droplet Digital PCR, electrophoresis and imaging systems, plus diagnostic tests for blood typing, diabetes and infectious diseases, sold to hospitals, labs, universities and biopharma worldwide. Revenue is around $2.5 billion to $2.8 billion with about 8,000 employees. B2B brand well known in labs, not among consumers.

Charles River Laboratories is a US contract research organisation based in Wilmington, Massachusetts, and listed on the NYSE (CRL), founded in 1947. It provides preclinical drug discovery and safety testing services, research animal models, and manufacturing support services to pharma and biotech companies, regulators and academic labs in about 20 countries. Revenue is about $4 billion with 20,000 employees. Well known in the pharma industry, with no consumer awareness.

Ginkgo Bioworks is a US synthetic biology company based in Boston and listed on the NYSE (DNA), going public through a SPAC merger in 2021. It runs automated cell programming laboratories (foundries) and offers a platform to design and engineer microbes and enzymes for pharma, agriculture, food and industrial customers on a fee and milestone basis. It also provides biosecurity services. Revenue is around $200 million a year, with large losses. Well known in biotech, but not to consumers.

Immunocore is a UK biotechnology company based in Abingdon, Oxfordshire, and listed on Nasdaq (IMCR). It develops T cell receptor bispecific immunotherapies, with its approved drug Kimmtrak (tebentafusp) for uveal melanoma, a rare eye cancer, sold in the US and Europe, plus pipeline programmes in other cancers and autoimmune disease. Customers are oncologists and hospitals. Revenue is a few hundred million dollars, with total funding of about $1.2 billion. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand awareness.

Kura Oncology is a US clinical and commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company based in San Diego and listed on Nasdaq (KURA). It develops targeted oral cancer drugs, led by ziftomenib, a menin inhibitor for acute myeloid leukemia with NPM1 mutations, and farnesyl transferase inhibitor tipifarnib. Customers are oncologists and hospitals. It has total funding of about $1.2 billion and is early in commercialisation. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand profile.

about: Iovance Biotherapeutics is a US biotechnology company based in San Carlos, California, and listed on Nasdaq (IOVA). It developed Amtagvi (lifileucel), the first tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) cell therapy, approved by the FDA in February 2024 for advanced melanoma, and is testing it in lung and other cancers. Customers are specialist cancer centres, with each treatment made from a patient's own cells. Revenue is early stage, with funding of about $1.6 billion shown. Known to oncologists and investors only.

New Amsterdam Pharma is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company with Dutch roots, listed on Nasdaq (NAMS), focused on cardiovascular disease. Its lead drug, obicetrapib, is an oral CETP inhibitor designed to lower LDL cholesterol in patients with heart disease or high cholesterol, developed with partner Menarini in Europe. It raised about $1.2 billion in total funding and has no approved product yet. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand profile.

about: Oxford Nanopore Technologies is a UK life sciences company based in Oxford and listed on the London Stock Exchange (ONT) since its 2021 IPO. It makes nanopore DNA and RNA sequencing devices, including the pocket-size MinION and the high-throughput PromethION, sold to research labs, public health agencies, pharma and clinical customers, and used in COVID-19 genomic surveillance. Founded in 2005, it has revenue of about 180 to 200 million pounds and is loss-making. Respected in science, with no consumer brand awareness.

Verona Pharma was a UK-founded respiratory biopharmaceutical company, with offices in London and Raleigh, whose product Ohtuvayre (ensifentrine) was approved by the FDA in 2024 as a nebulised maintenance treatment for COPD. It was listed on Nasdaq. Merck agreed to buy Verona in 2025 for around $10 billion, so it is now part of Merck. Customers are pulmonologists, pharmacies and COPD patients in the US. Specialist pharma with no consumer brand awareness.

Akero Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in South San Francisco, developing efruxifermin, an FGF21 analogue for treating metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), a serious fatty liver disease. It was listed on Nasdaq, and in late 2025 Novo Nordisk agreed to acquire it for a deal worth several billion dollars. It had no approved product or revenue. Funding of about $951 million is shown. B2B pharma with no consumer brand profile.

Bicycle Therapeutics is a UK-founded biotechnology company based in Cambridge, listed on Nasdaq (BCYC), with a US office in Lexington, Massachusetts. It develops Bicycle peptide therapeutics, small constrained peptides with antibody-like binding, including toxin conjugates against solid tumours such as zelenectide pevedotin. It earns collaboration revenue from partners such as Genentech, Novartis and Bayer. Total funding of about $1.1 billion is shown. Clinical-stage, with no consumer brand profile.

It grows by acquiring brands from larger pharma groups and supplying them to hospitals and pharmacies. It is backed by private capital, with funding of about 900 million shown for late 2024. B2B pharma with no consumer brand profile.

about: Establishment Labs is a medical technology company based in Alajuela, Costa Rica, and listed on Nasdaq (ESTA). It makes Motiva breast implants, which use its SmoothSilk surface, plus minimally invasive aesthetic devices, and sells them through surgeons in more than 80 countries, with the US as the key growth market after FDA approval in 2024. Revenue is roughly $160 million to $170 million. Surgeons are the buyers; patients know the Motiva brand in aesthetics but it has low general public awareness.

Eurofins Scientific is a Luxembourg-based testing and laboratory services group, listed on Euronext Paris and controlled by the Martin family. It runs hundreds of labs in about 60 countries, testing food, environment, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics and clinical samples, as well as genomics and diagnostics. Revenue is about 6.5 billion to 7 billion euros with some 60,000 employees. Customers are producers, retailers, pharma and regulators. B2B brand known in industry, not to consumers.

Gentiva is a US home health, hospice and personalised care provider headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, one of the largest hospice operators in the country with hundreds of locations across many states. It provides nursing, therapy and end-of-life care in patients' homes, funded mainly by Medicare. It is private, owned by Clayton, Dubilier and Rice, and combined with Kindred at Home. Funding of $900 million is shown. Healthcare services provider with limited brand awareness outside its sector.

about: Geron is a US biopharmaceutical company based in Foster City, California, and listed on Nasdaq (GERN). Its product Rytelo (imetelstat), a telomerase inhibitor approved by the FDA in June 2024, treats lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) with transfusion-dependent anaemia, and is sold to haematologists in the US, with a European launch. Revenue is early stage, with funding of about $1 billion shown. Specialist pharma with no consumer brand awareness.

Janux Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotechnology company based in San Diego and listed on Nasdaq (JANX). It has no approved products and earns small collaboration revenue. Total funding of about $900 million is shown. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand profile.

LANXESS is a German specialty chemicals group based in Cologne, listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, created in 2004 from Bayer's chemicals business. It makes additives, intermediates, flame retardants, lubricant additives and high-performance materials for automotive, construction, agriculture, water treatment and consumer end markets, with revenue of about 6.5 billion euros and some 13,000 employees. It holds naming rights to Cologne's LANXESS arena and has sponsored Borussia Dortmund. B2B brand with strong corporate recognition in Germany.

Novocure is a Swiss-incorporated oncology device company, with operations in Baar, Switzerland, and Portsmouth, New Hampshire, listed on Nasdaq (NVCS). Its Optune system delivers Tumor Treating Fields, electrical fields applied through a wearable device on the patient's skin to slow cancer cell division, approved for glioblastoma and mesothelioma, with trials in pancreatic and lung cancers. Revenue is roughly $600 million with funding of about $1.1 billion. Known to oncologists and patients, with limited public brand awareness.

AtaiBeckley is a US biopharmaceutical company based in New York, listed on Nasdaq (ATAI), formed by the combination of atai Life Sciences and Beckley Psytech in 2025. It develops short-acting psychedelic-derived treatments for mental health disorders, including mebufotenin (5-MeO-DMT) for depression and DMT-based programmes. It is clinical stage with no revenue from products and total funding of about $800 million. Known to investors in the psychedelics sector, with no consumer profile.

about: X4 Pharmaceuticals is a US biopharmaceutical company based in Boston and listed on Nasdaq (XFOR). Customers are immunologists and rare disease patients. Funding of about $760 million is shown. Specialist pharma with no consumer brand profile.

Acadia Healthcare is a US behavioural health provider based in Franklin, Tennessee, and listed on Nasdaq (ACHC). It is the largest standalone operator of psychiatric hospitals and addiction treatment centres in the country, with roughly 250 to 260 facilities and some 10,000 beds. Revenue is about 3 billion dollars, mostly from Medicare, Medicaid and insurers. It has been through legal scrutiny of admission practices. Healthcare provider brand with limited consumer awareness.

Alltech is a private animal health and nutrition company based in Nicholasville, Kentucky, founded in 1980 by Dr Pearse Lyons. It makes feed supplements, yeast products and mineral nutrition for livestock and pets, with operations in over 100 countries, and runs the Lexington Brewing and Distilling Company producing Kentucky Ale and Town Branch bourbon. Revenue is about 2 billion dollars. It was title sponsor of the FEI World Equestrian Games in 2010 and 2018. B2B brand with some consumer-facing drinks and equestrian profile.

Belite Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in San Diego, listed on Nasdaq (BLTE), with research ties to Taiwan. Its lead drug tinlarebant is an oral therapy to reduce vitamin A dimer build-up in the eye, in trials for Stargardt disease and geographic atrophy, an advanced form of dry age-related macular degeneration. It has no approved products. Funding of about $589 million is shown. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand profile.

about: Evolus is a US medical aesthetics company based in Newport Beach, California, and listed on Nasdaq (EOLS). It markets Jeuveau (prabotulinumtoxinA), a botulinum toxin competing with Botox for frown lines, and, from 2024, the Evolysse range of hyaluronic acid fillers, selling to aesthetic physicians in the US, Europe and Canada. Its Jeuveau is made by South Korea's Daewoong. Revenue is about 270 million dollars. Branded to consumers through marketing campaigns, so it has moderate public awareness.

Insulet is a US medical device company based in Acton, Massachusetts, and listed on Nasdaq (PODD). Its Omnipod system is a tubeless, wearable insulin pump with an automated insulin delivery algorithm for people with type 1 and type 2 diabetes, sold through pharmacies and distributors in the US and about two dozen other countries. Revenue is around 2 billion dollars and growing. Strong brand among people with diabetes and clinicians, with growing consumer recognition.

Ipsen is a French specialty biopharmaceutical group based in Paris, listed on Euronext Paris and controlled by the Beaufour family. It sells Dysport (botulinum toxin), Somatuline, Onivyde and Cabometyx outside the US, and rare disease drugs such as Bylvay, in oncology, neuroscience and rare diseases, in more than 100 countries. Revenue is about 3 billion euros with roughly 5,000 employees. B2B pharma with strong standing among physicians and limited public awareness.

Jubilant Bhartia Group is an Indian conglomerate based in Noida, led by Shyam and Hari Bhartia. Its holdings include Jubilant FoodWorks, the master franchisee of Domino's Pizza in India and also Dunkin' and other restaurant brands, Jubilant Pharmova (pharma and radiopharmacy), Jubilant Ingrevia (specialty chemicals) and Jubilant Agri. The group has multiple listed companies and revenue in the billions of dollars. Domino's India gives it strong consumer recognition.

Lyell Immunopharma is a US clinical-stage cell therapy company based in South San Francisco, listed on Nasdaq (LYEL). It develops CAR-T cell therapies for solid and blood cancers, led by rondecabtagene autoleucel (ronde-cel) for large B-cell lymphoma, using its own cell manufacturing capability. It has no approved product. Funding of about $593 million is shown. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand awareness.

It is partnered with Bristol Myers Squibb on cell therapies. It has no approved product. Funding of about $558 million is shown. Specialist biotech with no consumer brand profile.
